Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration (streaming, function-calling, embeddings)

Thanks for the productive call today 

d





QRECAP and next steps from our side.

Key pain points you called out:
- Real-time streaming latency spikes when generating structured JSON outputs for agent UI (esp. during high concurrency).
- Need high-quality embeddings for reranking search results; current embeddings are inconsistent across product content types.
- Desire for function-calling / structured outputs so downstream services can reliably parse and act on model responses.

What we heard as goals:
- 50% reduction in tail latency for streaming responses under typical load.
- 10-20% improvement in reranking precision by replacing current embedding pipeline.
- Minimal SDK changes for your frontend engineers (preferable: patch-level changes, not full refactor).

Product / integration fit (initial):
- Streaming: Redwood Streaming endpoints with prefix/KV caching should reduce token generation latency; we recommend conservative chunk sizes to start (200-400 tokens) and incremental increases.
- Function calling / structured outputs: Redwood supports function/tool calling patterns and structured JSON output enforcement; we can ship structured output schemas and validate at the runtime layer.
- Embeddings & reranking: recommend running a benchmark with our suggested embedding model (text-embed-1-large) and a small reranker test set - we can run a 2-week trial cluster for this.

Attachments: attached integration diagram and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP). Ethan will follow up with a sample config for your infra team.

Next steps / owners:
1) Technical deep-dive (Ethan) - dive into SDK changes, sample config, and streaming params. Target: 7/13 or 7/14.
2) Security/compliance checklist (Marissa) - send SOC2 + SSO details and evidence. Target: by 7/10.
3) Benchmark plan for embeddings (Marissa + Acme) - sample dataset and evaluation metrics. Target: draft by 7/15.

If that matches your notes, I’ll send calendar invites for the TD and put together the MAP with milestones.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi John / Sarah - Ethan from Redwood SE team here. Quick technical notes ahead of the TD: 

1) Schema enforcement: Redwood runtime can be configured to enforce structured outputs using a strict parser + validation step. We can do either: 
   - "Hard fail" (return a specific error code + no partial output) or
   - "Best-effort with flag" (return output + a metadata flag indicating validation status).
We recommend starting with "best-effort with flag" for production to avoid user-visible failures, then flip to "hard fail" during a controlled rollout.

2) Streaming: For your use-case (lots of small agent interactions), use continuous streaming with prefix caching. Start with chunk_size=300 tokens and max_concurrency per session set to 8. We'll monitor tail latency and tune kernel/quantization if needed.

3) SDK changes: We aim for patch-level changes. Example minimal change: update to redwood-js v2.1 which adds function-calling helpers and built-in streaming events. We'll provide a migration diff and a sample config (attached: redwood-sample-config.yaml).

4) Embeddings: recommend running a 1k-item benchmark with text-embed-1-large and kNN reranking (k=10). We can host a temporary trial index and provide evaluation metrics (recall@10, MRR).

I’ve attached a sample config and will bring a more detailed checklist to the TD.

--Ethan
